sentences.text: What happens when a giant star dies?

shots.title: HOW BLACK HOLES ARE FORMED

shots.image_prompt: Inside a glowing star-forming nebula, dense clouds of red and blue hydrogen gas with newborn stars
shots.motion_prompt: a newborn star ignites and flares brightly inside the gas cloud, glowing gas swirls around it, slow camera push in

sentences.text: Every black hole begins its life as a star,

shots.image_prompt: A giant blue-white star shining brightly in deep space, glowing corona, lens flare
shots.motion_prompt: the star shines and slowly rotates, its glowing corona shimmering and flickering, camera slowly orbits around it

shots.image_prompt: Scientific visualization of a star cut open, a blazing white-hot core at the centre surrounded by glowing layers
shots.motion_prompt: bright waves of energy pulse outward from the blazing core through the glowing layers, rhythmic pulsing light

sentences.text: Deep in its core, nuclear fusion pushes outward,

shots.image_prompt: Close view of the surface of a giant star, boiling plasma granulation and arcing prominences, black space at the edges
shots.motion_prompt: the plasma surface churns and boils, glowing prominences arc and fall back onto the star, camera slowly pushes in

sentences.text: balancing the crushing pull of gravity.

shots.image_prompt: An enormous red supergiant star filling most of the frame, with a tiny yellow Sun-like star beside it for scale, deep space
shots.motion_prompt: slow camera pull back revealing the enormous size of the red supergiant next to the tiny yellow star, the supergiant's surface churning

sentences.text: But in a star more than about twenty times heavier than the Sun,

shots.image_prompt: Scientific visualization of a dying star cut open, its core turning dull dark grey and heavy, outer layers dimming
shots.motion_prompt: the glow of the core fades and dims, the centre turns dark grey and heavy, flickering light dying out

sentences.text: the fuel eventually runs out, and the core fills with iron.

shots.image_prompt: The core of a massive star at the moment of collapse, layers of glowing gas falling inward toward a tiny bright centre
shots.motion_prompt: the star's layers rapidly implode and rush inward toward the centre, violent fast collapse, camera shaking slightly

sentences.text: With nothing left to hold it up, the core collapses in less than a second,

shots.image_prompt: A massive star exploding as a supernova, a brilliant flash of white light at the centre, shock waves of glowing gas
shots.motion_prompt: a gigantic supernova explosion bursts outward, brilliant flash, shock waves of glowing gas racing toward the camera, debris flying

sentences.text: and the outer layers can be blasted away in a supernova.

shots.image_prompt: An expanding supernova remnant, glowing red and teal gas filaments around a tiny bright collapsing point at the centre
shots.motion_prompt: the glowing debris cloud expands outward while the tiny bright point at the centre shrinks and collapses, slow push in

sentences.text: If the leftover core weighs more than about three Suns, no known force can stop its collapse.

shots.image_prompt: A newly formed black hole in deep space, a perfectly black sphere with a thin bright ring of light around it
shots.motion_prompt: a glowing accretion disk begins to swirl around the black sphere, light bending around the edge, slow camera push in

sentences.text: It falls in on itself, hidden behind an event horizon,

shots.image_prompt: A black hole with a bright orange accretion disk, gravitational lensing bending the light of background stars
shots.motion_prompt: streams of light curve and spiral into the black hole and vanish, the accretion disk slowly rotating, very slow push in

sentences.text: a boundary from which not even light can escape.

shots.image_prompt: A row of large radio telescope dishes on a high desert plateau at night under a sky full of stars and the Milky Way
shots.motion_prompt: time-lapse: the telescope dishes slowly turn together to point at the sky while the stars wheel overhead

sentences.text: In 2019, astronomers released the first image of a black hole's shadow, in the galaxy M87.
sentences.tts: In twenty nineteen, astronomers released the first image of a black hole's shadow, in the galaxy M eighty-seven.

shots.image_prompt: A spiral galaxy seen from far away, a bright glowing core at its centre, billions of stars and dark dust lanes
shots.motion_prompt: slow cinematic flight toward the glowing core of the spiral galaxy, the galaxy slowly rotating

sentences.text: And how the giant black holes at the centres of galaxies formed is still one of astronomy's great open questions.

claims.text: Stars are powered by nuclear fusion in their cores; the outward pressure balances gravity.
Stars of roughly twenty or more solar masses can end as black holes; the exact threshold depends on the star and is uncertain, so the script says 'about'.
Fusion stops at iron; the iron core collapses in under a second; many (not all) such collapses produce a supernova.
A collapsed core above roughly 2-3 solar masses cannot be supported as a neutron star and becomes a black hole.
Nothing, including light, escapes from inside the event horizon.
The Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of a black hole's shadow (M87*) in April 2019.
How supermassive black holes formed is an open research question.
